name: SpeedRadialBlur
src_typeComment: Drop on the MAIN CAMERA for a full-screen "going fast" radial blur that eases in/out with speed — call SetSpeed01(0..1) every frame from whatever drives the vehicle/character's actual speed (e.g. rigidbody.velocity.magnitude / topSpeed). A camera image-effect (OnRenderImage), the classic Built-in RP way to do a full-screen post-process — genuinely costs a full extra Blit pass across the whole screen, which is the deliberate trade for the most immersive version of this effect (a cheaper stylized speed-line overlay is a different tool for when that cost isn't worth it).

src_serialized.name: maxBlurAmount
src_serialized.tooltip: Blur strength at full speed (speed01 = 1), as a fraction of the screen. 0.08-0.15 is a reasonable range before it gets disorienting.

src_serialized.name: smoothing
src_serialized.tooltip: Higher = the blur reacts to a speed change more quickly; lower = more lag easing in/out.

src_members.sig: public void SetSpeed01(float speed01) => targetSpeed01 = Mathf.Clamp01(speed01)
src_members.name: SetSpeed01
src_members.comment: 0 = stationary (no blur), 1 = full speed (maxBlurAmount). Values outside [0,1] are clamped, so feeding a raw speed/topSpeed ratio that can briefly exceed 1 (e.g. a boost) is safe as-is.

src_members.name: Tick
src_members.comment: The actual smoothing logic, pulled out of Update() so it can be driven deterministically by a self- test — Time.deltaTime is meaningless outside Play mode, and OnRenderImage never fires outside an actual camera render pass either, so this is the one piece of the effect a headless test CAN drive.
